issues.description: PersonResource#getAllPersons declares a different collection generic type than the service it invokes. In the template, PersonResource.getAllPersons returns ResponseEntity<List<Person>> and PersonService.getAll() returns List<Person>. In the solution, PersonResource.getAllPersons is changed to ResponseEntity<Set<Person>> but still calls personService.getAll() which returns List<Person>. This generic type mismatch is structural and would cause compilation errors or confusion for students comparing template, tests, and solution.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the return types consistent. Option A: Change PersonResource.getAllPersons to return ResponseEntity<List<Person>> (matching PersonService.getAll()). Option B: Change PersonService.getAll() to return Set<Person> and adapt its implementation to convert the repository result (e.g., new HashSet<>(personRepository.findAll())). Ensure any tests and other usages match the chosen collection type.

issues.description: The return type for the conceptual "get all persons" endpoint is inconsistent across artifacts: the TEMPLATE repository's PersonResource defines getAllPersons() as returning ResponseEntity<List<Person>> while the SOLUTION repository's PersonResource defines it as ResponseEntity<Set<Person>>. Additionally, in the SOLUTION repository PersonService.getAll() returns List<Person>, which mismatches the SOLUTION PersonResource return type. This creates a mapping confusion for students (should the API expose a List or a Set?) and may introduce compilation or integration issues in the solution code.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the collection type consistent across artifacts: either (A) change both PersonResource implementations to return ResponseEntity<List<Person>> and ensure PersonService.getAll() returns List<Person>, or (B) change PersonService.getAll() to return Set<Person> and adapt repository/service code accordingly. Update any tests and documentation to use the chosen collection type so students have a single, unambiguous target.
